# Results — Study 737 (Sunspot-Cycle)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
William Stanley Jevons's (1878) sunspot theory of the trade cycle, in its surviving
**"the stock market runs on an ~11-year solar clock"** form: high solar activity →
good returns, low activity → bad. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`74635b6681a5` (^GSPC daily) / `a26d426a3204` (^GSPC monthly).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **^GSPC — the S&P 500 PRICE index** (24,740 daily rows, 1927-12-30 → 2026-06-30; 1,183 monthly rows). **Price-only** (no dividends) — labelled as such everywhere, never called total return. Chosen deliberately for **length**: no total-return equity series reaches back ten solar cycles, and an 11-year cyclicality cannot live in a dividend stream |
| Solar calendar | **hardcoded** table of solar cycles **16 → 25** (`SOLAR_CYCLES`), each cycle's minimum date, maximum date and SILSO v2 smoothed peak sunspot number, keyed from the WDC-SILSO (Royal Observatory of Belgium) / NOAA-SWPC published record. Cycle 25's maximum (2024-10) and amplitude are provisional at this as-of |
| Sunspot proxy | a **LABELLED cosine reconstruction** of the smoothed monthly sunspot number — phase 0 at each minimum, π at each maximum, activity `(1−cos φ)/2` scaled by the cycle's peak amplitude. A stand-in for *where in the 11-year cycle a month sits*, keyed to the published turning points — **not** the raw daily SILSO file, and named a proxy at every use |
| Events | **10** solar maxima and **9** solar minima land on the tape (the 1923-08 minimum predates it and is excluded, never snapped forward to the tape start) |
| Statistics | Two units, matched to two tests: **one-sample / Welch t across the 19 independent turning-point events** (≥ 5 yr apart → non-overlapping) for the forward-return study, each group vs a random-calendar placebo; for the autocorrelated monthly panel, **Newey-West (HAC, 12 lags)** t's on the phase regression and a **circular block bootstrap** (12-month blocks) on the regime spread, with a phase-shift placebo. Wilson intervals on hit rates |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: the solar-clock **timer** acts on the phase lagged **6 months** (the SILSO smoothing lag — a turning point is only *known* to be one once the smoothed number is published), long-or-flat, one-way cost × NAV per switch. The forward-return event study uses the *true* turning-point dates and is labelled **generous / retrospective** (perfect hindsight of the cycle you'd never have live) |

No survivorship concern (a single broad index, no cross-section). **Named on the Signal
axis:** the tape is **price-only** (the dividend yield is missing from every return here);
this cannot create or destroy an 11-year period, but every return figure is a price
return, not a total return.

## H₁ — the 11-year wave (phase regression, HAC)

Regress monthly abnormal returns on `(1, cos φ, sin φ)`.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| R² (variance explained by the 11-year wave) | **0.360%** |
| cos coefficient, HAC *t* | **+1.04** |
| sin coefficient, HAC *t* | **+1.83** |
| fitted sinusoid amplitude | **554 bps/yr** |

The 11-year cycle explains **about 1 part in 280** of monthly return variation, and
neither harmonic clears the |*t*| ≥ 2 desk bar. Even taking the point estimate at face
value, the entire predicted top-to-bottom swing is ~554 bps/yr — dwarfed by the market's
own monthly volatility. **H₁ not supported.**

## H₂ — active vs quiet Sun (regime split)

High-activity (top tercile) vs low-activity (bottom tercile) months.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| high-activity mean | **+0.441%/mo** (n = 387) |
| low-activity mean | **+1.002%/mo** (n = 387) |
| high − low spread | **−673 bps/yr** |
| block-bootstrap 95% CI (monthly) | **[−1.378%, +0.271%]** |
| block-bootstrap two-sided *p* | **0.179** |
| phase-shift placebo *p* (5,000 draws) | **0.095** |

The spread is **wrong-signed** for the claim — the market does slightly *worse* when the
Sun is active — and it is not even a real negative: a random 11-year clock (phase-shift
placebo) produces a spread this large about **one time in ten**. **H₂ rejected on sign,
unsupported on magnitude.**

## H₃ — turning points: forward 12-month return after maxima vs minima

Independent events (≥ 5 yr apart); each group's mean placed against a random-calendar
placebo of the same size (the market's up-drift makes *any* set of dates look positive).

| group | n | mean fwd-12m | one-sample *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) | random-calendar *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| after solar **MAX** (the claim's boom) | 10 | **+5.63%** | +0.74 | 6/10 [31.3%, 83.2%] | 0.663 |
| after solar **MIN** | 9 | **+18.91%** | **+3.33** | 7/9 [45.3%, 93.7%] | **0.054** |
| any random year (unconditional) | — | **+8.17%** | — | — | — |

The **maximum** — where the claim predicts the boom — returns **+5.63%** (*t* = 0.74),
*below* the +8.17% you'd get on a random year. The **minimum** is the study's lone
|*t*| ≥ 2, but it is a trap on three counts: (i) it points the **wrong way** for the
claim (Jevons says peaks are good, not troughs); (ii) that fat one-sample *t* merely
re-discovers that the market drifts up over *any* 9 dates — measured against a random
9-date calendar it is only **p = 0.054**; (iii) it rests on 9 events, a few of which
(1954, 1986, 2008) happen to sit near market bottoms. The **max − min** contrast is
**Welch *t* = −1.39**, also wrong-signed. **H₃ rejected.**

## H₄ — the solar-clock timer

Long the index when the *lagged* phase is rising (min→max), else cash; the phase is
lagged **6 months** (the SILSO smoothing lag — one documented lag, applied once); costs
one-way × NAV per switch; long-or-flat; vs buy-and-hold on the identical window.

| one-way cost | timer CAGR | buy & hold | excess | excess *t* | Sharpe (timer / B&H) | exposure |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | **3.10%/yr** | 6.23%/yr | **−3.13 pp** | **−2.65** | 0.37 / 0.42 | 38% |
| 5 bps | **3.09%/yr** | 6.23%/yr | −3.14 pp | −2.66 | 0.37 / 0.42 | 38% |
| 10 bps | **3.07%/yr** | 6.23%/yr | −3.15 pp | −2.67 | 0.36 / 0.42 | 38% |

The timer **halves** buy-and-hold's return and does so at *t* = −2.65 (significantly
*worse*), with a lower Sharpe too — and the costs barely matter (20 switches over 98
years). It loses by sitting in cash through the quiet half of a market that drifts up
regardless of the Sun. **H₄ not supported; there is no edge to charge costs against.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic monthly tape phased to the *real* solar calendar, with a TUNABLE planted
solar-cycle return term; no network.

| world | regime split |
|---|--:|
| null (amp = 0), **20 seeds** | mean *p* = **0.47**, *p* < 0.05 in **1/20 seeds** (≈ the 5% expected) |
| planted cycle (amp = 2%), seed 737 | spread **−3,970 bps/yr**, *p* < 0.001, phase R² = **11.4%**, cos *t* = **14.5** |

The detector never systematically fires on the null and lights up sharply on a planted
cycle — so the empty real-tape result is a genuine reading, not a sleepy detector. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The 11-year phase regression explains **R² = 0.36%** of monthly
  returns, both HAC *t* < 2; the active−quiet regime spread is **−673 bps/yr**
  (wrong-signed, block-boot *p* = 0.179, placebo *p* = 0.095); the max−min turning-point
  contrast is Welch *t* = −1.39 (wrong-signed). The lone |*t*| ≥ 2 (forward return after
  solar minima, *t* = +3.33) is a wrong-signed, n = 9 look-elsewhere artifact that is
  only *p* = 0.054 against a random calendar.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A lag-honest solar-clock timer earns **3.1%/yr** vs
  buy-and-hold's **6.2%/yr** (excess *t* = −2.65), a lower Sharpe, before costs bite.
- **"Jevons's sunspot cycle in the market?" — BUSTED.** On ten solar cycles of the
  longest S&P tape available — an *exogenous, known-in-advance* calendar with no
  reverse-causation or date-mining escape hatch, given every benefit of the doubt —
  there is no 11-year clock in equity returns. This says nothing about the sunspot cycle
  itself (which is real); only that the *market* does not run on it.
